title: fix(android): external signer notification recovery
body: ## Upstream Dependency Resolved: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#811 has merged, and this PR points at the merged `whitenoise-rs` master revision `49e5f20c43fd72f1d07ea3675350754650955371`. ## Summary - Fix Android background notifications for multi-account external-signer users after reboot / headless foreground-service startup. - Reconcile external signer callbacks from both the UI isolate and foreground-task isolate so every persisted external-signer account has a live callback before notification handling begins. - Register external signer callbacks before ensuring Rust relay subscriptions and before attaching the headless notification stream. - Register app-local Android plugins with the headless foreground-task Flutter engine so the Android signer method channel is available outside `MainActivity`. - Keep headless notification subscriptions from requesting notification permission when no Activity is attached. - Keep the foreground service configured with the `dataSync` service type without restarting an already-running service on every cold start. - Make external signer reconciliation best-effort for non-active accounts while preserving fast-fail behavior for the activating account. ## Review Follow-up - Renamed the lifecycle helper from `ExternalSignerRegistrationService` to `ExternalSignerCallbackRegistry` to make the split from `AndroidSignerService` clearer. - Added Android platform guards in both the callback registry and `AndroidSignerService.registerExternalSigner`. - Removed the short-pubkey logging helper that implied invalid pubkeys were expected. - Removed the `@visibleForTesting` entry point from `NotificationTaskHandler`; tests now exercise retry behavior through task start/repeat/coordination events. - Removed the process-local foreground-service restart flag that would stop/start a running service on every cold start. - Collapsed foreground-task subscription tracking to the subscription source of truth, and clear `NotificationSubscription.isRunning` when the stream closes. - Left the local-account concern as code-is: reconciliation filters `AccountType.external_` before registration, and mixed local/external account tests cover that path. ## Root Cause The boot/reboot foreground task was alive and subscribed to the Rust notification stream, but it did not have external-signer callbacks registered in that headless Dart isolate. Incoming events for Amber-backed accounts could arrive and be persisted, but Rust could not fully process/decrypt them into notification updates until the main app isolate opened and `authProvider` registered the signer callbacks. The desired runtime state is now reconciled in both isolates: every signed-in external-signer account has a registered signer callback in the current process/isolate before notification handling begins. ## Manual Verification Verified on a Pixel 7 Pro with two Amber-backed accounts and a second Android sender device: - Rebooted the Amber device. - Waited for the silent `White Noise connected to relays` foreground notification. - Sent messages to both Amber-backed accounts before opening White Noise. - Both Android notifications appeared while the app remained unopened. - Logs showed the expected order: system foreground task start, external signer callback registration for both accounts, Rust relay subscription ensure, notification stream subscription, received notification updates, displayed notifications. ## Testing - `flutter test --reporter compact test/services/android_signer_service_test.dart test/services/external_signer_callback_registry_test.dart test/services/foreground_service_test.dart test/providers/auth_provider_test.dart` - `just test-flutter-quiet` - `just precommit` - Earlier Android validation: `just when-apk` plus install/manual reboot testing on physical devices. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Release Notes * **New Features** * External signer callback registration is now automatically triggered when the app resumes. * **Improvements** * Enhanced external signer account reconciliation across login, logout, and profile-switching flows. * Notification permission requests are now optional and configurable. * Improved Android foreground service lifecycle handling and coordination. * **Tests** * Expanded test coverage for external signer registration, app lifecycle, and notification handling.

title: WnSystemNotice: 'Null check operator used on a null value' from auto-hide Timer firing after dispose
body:
## Symptom

A user's logcat shows an unhandled Dart exception during a flow that surfaces a `WnSystemNotice` toast and then quickly transitions away from the screen:

\`\`\`
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : [ERROR:flutter/runtime/dart_vm_initializer.cc(40)]
                                Unhandled Exception: Null check operator used on a null value
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #0  AnimationController.stop
                                    (package:flutter/src/animation/animation_controller.dart:899)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #1  AnimationController._animateToInternal
                                    (package:flutter/src/animation/animation_controller.dart:673)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #2  AnimationController.reverse
                                    (package:flutter/src/animation/animation_controller.dart:521)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #3  WnSystemNotice.build.handleDismiss
                                    (package:whitenoise/widgets/wn_system_notice.dart:111)
05-08 15:55:19.420  E flutter : #4  Timer._createTimer.<anonymous closure>
                                    (dart:async-patch/timer_patch.dart:18)
\`\`\`

It happened during a rapid sequence of three failed \"Add to group\" attempts (~3 s apart) where each surfaced an error toast and the user navigated between screens. The auto-hide Timer for a previous toast fired against a controller whose ticker had already been nulled out — `AnimationController.stop` reads `_ticker!` which throws when the controller has been disposed.

## Suspected cause

`lib/widgets/wn_system_notice.dart`:

\`\`\`dart
105    final autoHideTimer = useRef<Timer?>(null);
106
107    void handleDismiss() {
108      if (isDismissing.value) return;
109      isDismissing.value = true;
110      autoHideTimer.value?.cancel();
111      slideController.reverse().then((_) {        // <-- crash site
112        onDismiss?.call();
113      });
114    }

125    useEffect(() {
126      final duration = autoHideDuration ?? (_isTemporary ? _defaultAutoHideDuration : null);
127      if (duration != null && onDismiss != null) {
128        autoHideTimer.value = Timer(duration, handleDismiss);
129      }
130      return () => autoHideTimer.value?.cancel();
131    }, [autoHideDuration, _isTemporary, onDismiss]);
\`\`\`

The cleanup on line 130 cancels the Timer on dispose / dep change. But there is at least one window where the Timer has already fired and `handleDismiss` is queued (or running) before the cleanup runs — at that point `slideController.reverse()` executes against a disposed controller and `AnimationController.stop`'s `_ticker!` blows up.

There may also be a longer-running variant: `handleDismiss` fires *before* dispose, kicks off `slideController.reverse()`, and the widget is dismounted while the reverse animation is still ticking — same crash, different phase of the same bug.

## Suggested fix directions

1. **Guard `handleDismiss` against a disposed controller.** `AnimationController` has no public `isDisposed`, but we can capture a `mounted`-style flag with a `useRef<bool>` set to `false` in a cleanup, and bail out of `handleDismiss` if not mounted. (Or use the `useIsMounted` hook from `flutter_hooks` directly — that's exactly what it's for.)
2. **Don't capture a stale `handleDismiss`.** The Timer at line 128 captures the closure from the first build. A small refactor — extract `handleDismiss` into a `useCallback` and have the Timer invoke through a stable indirection — keeps the cancel/dismiss pair in sync across rebuilds.
3. **Wrap the `.then(...)` chain.** Even if everything else is correct, `slideController.reverse().then(...)` is exposing dispose-during-animation. Use `vsync`-aware navigation guards or check status before calling `onDismiss`.

The minimum fix is probably (1) — wrap the body of `handleDismiss` in an `if (!isMounted()) return;` check.

## Repro

Hard to reproduce deterministically; the captured trace happened during this sequence:

1. Trigger an action that surfaces a `WnSystemNotice` error toast (e.g., the failing add-to-group flow that produced the surrounding log entries).
2. Within ~3 s, navigate away from the screen so the parent widget is dismounted while the toast's auto-hide Timer is still pending or its dismiss animation is mid-flight.
3. The Timer fires into a disposed controller — unhandled exception.

A targeted test: mount a `WnSystemNotice` with `autoHideDuration: Duration(milliseconds: 50)`, pump 30 ms, dispose the host widget, then `pump(100)` — should reproduce.

## Severity

Doesn't crash the app but produces an unhandled exception in the Dart VM and — depending on how Flutter's error zone is configured — may or may not bubble to FlutterError. Easy fix, worth doing.

## Source

Caught in a real user's logcat during an unrelated investigation. Same log surfaced the `whitenoise-rs` `add_members` issue: marmot-protocol/whitenoise-rs#813.

title: fix: preserve chat list state across screen remounts (#483)
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/f3757fc28c0f4949a066f4338316f1d54ce148f70322d769352aa5b94cafb459.png) Closes #483. Returning to the chat list flashed a loading spinner because go_router's `goNamed` disposes `ChatListScreen`, and on pop the `useChatList` hook re-subscribed to the stream with no cached data. So every back-navigation looked like a cold start. Cache the chat-list map (per pubkey + archived) and the blocked-pubkeys set (per pubkey) at module scope so they outlive widget disposal. `isLoading` now gates on whether an initial snapshot was ever received, not on the current stream's connection state. A remount renders the cached marmots immediately and updates lazily as new stream events arrive. Regression test in `test/hooks/use_chat_list_test.dart` reproduces the bug (fails on old code, passes on the fix). Screen-level test in `test/screens/chat_list_screen_test.dart` locks in the user-flow behavior. Test-side cache reset is wired into `MockWnApi.reset()` so individual test files keep their existing setUp. `just precommit` passes. Coverage 99.36%. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Chat data now persists when navigating back to the chat list from an individual conversation, eliminating unnecessary loading states. * Implemented session-based caching for chat lists and blocked contacts to prevent redundant network requests, improving navigation speed and reducing data usage.

title: Dismiss chat list search on swipe-back instead of closing app
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/3dbf71efd665c3c69001188af6b8d1dd8d18f6a4ae803d11851488397070d5d9.png) On Android (e.g. GrapheneOS), the swipe-back gesture used to evict the entire app even when the chat list search bar was open. Wrong target: back should dismiss in-screen state first. The fix wraps `ChatListScreen` in a `PopScope` that intercepts the gesture whenever the search header is revealed or the query field has text. On intercept it unfocuses the keyboard, clears the query, and collapses the header. Once search is no longer visible, back falls through to its normal route pop. To enable parent-driven dismissal, `WnChatList` now accepts an optional `headerOpenNotifier`. When provided, the screen owns the open/closed state and a `useEffect` inside `WnChatList` animates the reveal in response to external changes. Callers without the notifier keep the previous internal state. Tested with three new widget tests covering: header dismissal on back, query clear on back, and pass-through when no search is active. Coverage holds at 99.33%. The marmots wave goodbye to the search bar, not to the whole burrow. Closes #612 --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved back button behavior when search UI is active. Back button now closes the search header instead of exiting the entire screen, then closes the app on subsequent press. * Enhanced header visibility synchronization with improved animation control. * **Tests** * Added comprehensive test coverage for back navigation behavior with active search. * Added tests for header visibility control and scroll position management.

title: [Feature]: Android in-app notification when a new release is available on Zapstore

labels.name: Idea 💡
labels.description: Ideas of changes so we don't forget to re evaluate later

body:
## Status

A first version of this feature **already shipped on 2026-03-20** via PR #506 (closes #505). This issue tracks the gaps that remain.

## What shipped in #506

- Rust API `fetch_latest_zapstore_version()` queries `relay.zapstore.dev` for the kind:32267 software application event for `org.parres.whitenoise`, follows the `a` tag to the kind:30063 release, and returns the version string.
- Flutter hook `useZapstoreUpdate` runs **on app start only** on Android, compares against installed `PackageInfo.version` using CalVer segment comparison.
- Dismissible info banner on the chat list with an "Update now" button that opens the Zapstore listing via `url_launcher`.
- Localized in 8 languages.

## What's still missing

The shipped version is the minimum viable banner. The following deltas still need work:

### 1. Publisher pubkey pinning (security)

`fetch_latest_zapstore_version()` queries kind:32267 by `d` tag (`org.parres.whitenoise`) without an `authors:` filter for the official White Noise publisher pubkey. Any Nostr key can publish a kind:32267 with the same `d` tag. If a malicious or compromised relay returns a spoofed event, the app will compare against an attacker-controlled version string.

**Fix**: hardcode the official White Noise publisher pubkey in the app and add it to the `authors:` filter on both kind:32267 and kind:30063 queries. Drop any event whose signature does not match.

This is the load-bearing security primitive for everything else here — until it lands, none of the items below should be expanded.

### 2. Periodic polling

Currently the check fires once per app start. A user who keeps the app open for days never re-checks.

**Proposal**: re-poll every 24 hours while the app is running, in addition to app start. Cache the latest seen version locally so we don't re-banner on the same release.

### 3. Escalation when far behind

The banner is uniformly dismissible regardless of how stale the build is. A user 5 releases behind sees the same low-key banner as someone 1 release behind.

**Proposal**:
- 0–2 releases behind: current dismissible banner (no change)
- 3+ releases behind: persistent, harder-to-dismiss banner with stronger copy. Re-show on every cold start until updated. The user is running a build that may be incompatible with the network — see #610 for an example of a backward-compat break across versions.

This requires knowing how many releases the user is behind, which requires either fetching the full `30063` release history or having Zapstore expose a counter. Implementation detail to be decided.

### 4. OS-level notification when backgrounded

The banner only shows once the user opens the app. If they haven't opened it in a week, they don't see anything.

**Proposal**: when the periodic poll fires and detects a new release, post a system notification (subject to the existing notification permission). Tapping it opens the chat list with the banner shown.

### 5. Settings row showing installed vs. latest

A user who dismisses the banner has no way to find their version-status again without checking Zapstore externally.

**Proposal**: add a row in Settings showing installed version, latest version, and how many releases behind. Tapping opens Zapstore. This is also a useful diagnostic field for support reports.

## iOS scope

iOS remains out of scope for the same reasons documented in the original issue:
- App Store: app updates are automatic by default. When users disable auto-update, the App Store notifies them. https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT202180
- TestFlight: the TestFlight app surfaces beta updates and supports automatic updates per build group. https://developer.apple.com/testflight/

Not tested on iOS — verification was via Apple's published documentation only.

## Test platform

GrapheneOS. All notification additions must respect the hardened permission model.

## Cross-reference

- Original problem statement: #505 (closed)
- First implementation: PR #506 (merged 2026-03-20)
- Auto-update follow-up: #622
